question: I have had a work permit in Sweden for four years and want to apply for permanent residence. My wife has a well-paid job and we have savings. Can her income or our savings count towards the maintenance requirement?
reference_answer: No. For permanent residence the applicant must be able to support themselves (5 kap. 7 § utlänningslagen), and in its legal position RS/084/2021 (section 3.1.1) Migrationsverket counts only income from the applicant's own employment or business, or both. A spouse's income does not count, even if it comes from employment, and neither do savings or someone else guaranteeing the applicant's support; benefits, grants, capital income, pension, unemployment benefit and activity support do not count either. The income must be taxed and legal, which means the applicant must have the right to work (a work permit or an exemption) at the time of the decision.
notes: Position paper RS/084/2021 v8.0, section 3.1.1 (Vilka inkomster kan tillgodoräknas). Agency interpretation of 5 kap. 7 §.

question: I want to apply for permanent residence. I have never been convicted of a crime, but I have some unpaid taxes and an unpaid fine. Can that stop me from getting permanent residence?
reference_answer: Yes, it can. Permanent residence requires that the applicant's expected conduct (vandel) gives no doubt (5 kap. 7 § utlänningslagen). In its legal position RS/084/2021 (section 3.2) Migrationsverket describes this as an overall, forward-looking assessment of the individual case that also considers how the person has lived, with no exhaustive list of disqualifying circumstances. Shortcomings that are not crimes can be enough on their own to refuse permanent residence; the paper gives unpaid taxes or fines as examples. Whether it is enough in a particular case depends on the overall assessment.
notes: Position paper RS/084/2021 v8.0, section 3.2 (Vandelskravet). The paper also cites MIG 2023:1 (assault five and a half years before the decision was enough to raise doubt).

question: My work permit expired last week and I forgot to apply for an extension in time. Can I still apply for an extension from Sweden, and can I keep working while it is processed?
reference_answer: An application made after the previous permit has expired is not an extension. In its legal position RS/082/2021 (section 2.3) Migrationsverket treats it as a new application, as if the person had entered Sweden and applied anew. The main rule is that a residence permit must be applied for and granted before entering Sweden (5 kap. 18 § första stycket utlänningslagen), so the application can be granted from inside Sweden only if one of the exceptions in 5 kap. 18 § applies; otherwise it is refused and a decision on refusal of entry or expulsion follows. Staying or working without the required permit can count against the application, and the person may be fined (RS/082/2021, section 2.4). Someone who did not apply before the previous permit ran out is, as a rule, not exempt from the work permit requirement while the application is processed, so they should not keep working (RS/084/2021, section 3.1.1, with reference to 5 kap. 3 § utlänningsförordningen).
notes: Position papers RS/082/2021 v5.0, sections 2.3–2.4, and RS/084/2021 v8.0, section 3.1.1 (working during processing). Agency interpretation.

question: My husband lives and works in Sweden and I am applying for a residence permit to join him. He recently started a new job at a small, newly started company. Does Migrationsverket look at his employer when it assesses whether he can support us?
reference_answer: Yes. Under 5 kap. 3 j § utlänningslagen the person in Sweden (the sponsor) must be able to support himself and the applicant. In its legal position RS/008/2026 (section 2.3.3.1) Migrationsverket says that this ability to support must last for some time, and that it therefore assesses the employer's seriousness and its ability to keep paying the salary over time, as the Migration Court of Appeal required for permanent residence in MIG 2023:4. A new job at a newly started company can therefore be examined more closely; whether the requirement is met depends on that assessment.
notes: Position paper RS/008/2026 v1.0, section 2.3.3.1 (Krav på arbetsgivares seriositet och förmåga att betala lön). Agency interpretation of 5 kap. 3 j §; the sponsor must meet the requirement (section 2.2.1).
